NO TD-059 STALL THIS ITERATION -- clean tree, implemented from scratch. First story in three not to inherit orphaned work. I still kept the US-526 ordering (gate -> COMMIT -> bookkeeping) because that ordering is what makes an iteration survivable, not a reaction to the stall.

*** THE AC WAS WRONG AND I DID NOT IMPLEMENT IT AS WRITTEN. *** AC1 said 'pull the exact good/degraded/replace DEPTH-BAND thresholds from Spool's ruling'. No such thing exists. Spool ruled the opposite verbatim: 'Bands UNCHANGED -- good >=582 s, degraded 436-582 s, replace <436 s, on RUNTIME_BASELINE_S = 727.' Only the GATE is depth-based. Inventing per-band voltages to satisfy the AC's phrasing would have been Rule-2 fabrication AND would have traded a reachability bug for a wrong-classification bug -- worse, because it looks like it works. I implemented the ruling, flagged the wording to Marcus in completionNotes, and fixed the same bad phrase where US-526 had leaked it into architecture.md. CARRY THIS: when an AC paraphrases an SME ruling, read the ruling -- the paraphrase is what drifts.

MUTATION TESTING CAUGHT MY OWN BAD TEST, and this is the reusable lesson. The gate is enforced TWICE (read SQL + _parseRow), so the halves cover for each other. My first boundary test asserted qualifyingCount/lastHealthCheckTs and its docstring CLAIMED it proved SQL filtered shallow rows. I neutralised the SQL predicate with `AND (end_vcell_v <= ? OR 1=1)` (param count preserved so nothing errored) and ALL 44 TESTS STILL PASSED -- the pure function silently covered for it, so a real SQL regression would ship green. Rewrote to assert at the READ BOUNDARY (monkeypatch computeBatteryHealthVerdict, capture exactly which rows SQL handed over); the same mutation now fails (4 rows crossed vs 3). GENERAL RULE FOR THIS CODEBASE: when a rule is enforced in two places, a test that asserts only on the RESULT tests neither half -- assert at the seam. Note the pre-existing sibling test_readBatteryHealthVerdict_appliesTheGateInSql has the identical blind spot.

Two further mutations proving the regression cannot return: floor 60->600 = 6 red (incl. the ordering guard + both band-reachability cases); depth 3.50->3.90 = 4 red (both boundaries). All three reverted + re-verified green. The reachability guard asserts the ORDERING (QUALIFYING_MIN_RUNTIME_S < DEGRADED < GOOD) not the literal 60 -- pinning `== 60` alone would let any future floor >= 436 s silently re-break reachability.

WHAT SHIPPED: QUALIFYING_MIN_RUNTIME_S 600 -> 60 (sanity floor only) + new QUALIFYING_MAX_END_VCELL_V = 3.50, in BOTH gate halves, with end_vcell_v SELECTed and carried across the read boundary. Bands/windows/staleness/median-of-3 untouched. US-504b's prediction held exactly -- 'only the gate constant moves' -- which is why the bands were parked in a separate public verdictForMedianRuntime().
